definition: Embodied cognitive science is an interdisciplinary field of research, the aim of which is to explain the mechanisms underlying intelligent behavior.
details: It comprises three main methodologies: the modeling of psychological and biological systems in a holistic manner that considers the mind and body as a single entity; the formation of a common set of general principles of intelligent behavior; and the experimental use of robotic agents in controlled environments.

explainer.lead: Embodied cognitive science studies intelligent behavior by treating the mind and body as one connected system. It combines holistic models, shared principles, and experiments with robots to explain how intelligence works.

tiers.eli5: Imagine learning to ride a bicycle: your thinking and your body’s movements work together, rather than acting as separate parts. Embodied cognitive science studies intelligence in that joined-up way. Researchers can also build robots and watch how they behave in carefully controlled settings.
tiers.practitioner: Apply it by modeling psychological or biological systems as integrated mind–body entities, then testing general principles of intelligent behavior with robotic agents in controlled environments. The work spans modeling, principle formation, and experimentation rather than prescribing a particular software stack. A key pitfall is treating the robot’s control system in isolation from its body.
tiers.paperLevel: Embodied cognitive science is an interdisciplinary research framework for explaining the mechanisms underlying intelligent behavior. Its three methodologies are holistic modeling of psychological and biological systems with mind and body treated as one entity, formulation of general principles of intelligent behavior, and controlled experiments using robotic agents. It is a methodological approach, not a single algorithm or equation.

explainer.example: Researchers could place a wheeled robot in a controlled room and study how it reaches a target. Instead of examining only its internal controller, they would treat its body, movements, and control processes as one system when explaining the behavior.

usedIn.name: Robotics research
usedIn.detail: Robotic agents are used experimentally in controlled environments.

usedIn.name: Psychology
usedIn.detail: Psychological systems are modeled holistically, with mind and body treated together.

usedIn.name: Biology
usedIn.detail: Biological systems provide another setting for holistic models of intelligent behavior.

explainer.intuition: Intelligence is examined through the whole behaving system, not through a mind treated as separate from its body. Models, general principles, and physical experiments offer complementary ways to explain that behavior.
howItWorks: Model a psychological or biological system as one mind–body entity.
Seek general principles that describe intelligent behavior.
Implement robotic agents for experimental investigation.
Test the agents in controlled environments.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a common research approach for connecting psychological and biological models with robotic experiments. Its aim is to uncover general mechanisms and principles of intelligent behavior.
misconceptions: It is not just robotics; robotic experiments are one of its three methodologies.
It does not treat the body as an optional container for an independent mind.
It is a research framework, not a single model or algorithm.

diagram.caption: The three methodologies combine holistic models, general principles, and robotic experiments to explain intelligent behavior.
